segments.text: Floating out in space, staring at the sun.
But right next to it, the sky is pitch black.
Sunlight scatters off tiny air molecules in every direction.
That's why Earth's sky glows bright all over.
But space barely has any air at all.
So there's nothing to scatter it, and the light just travels straight.
That's why only the sun's direction looks bright, and the rest stays pitch black.
